end.summary:
• Practised making one mark for each object to keep track without number names.
• Matched marks to objects to identify missing or extra items.
• Parth used a stone for each boat and checked leftover stones to find a boat that had not returned.
• They initially said a spread-out row had more objects; later paired each bindi with one bangle and said none were left over.
• They did not yet explain why one-to-one matching works without number names.
end.parentNote: Parth practised tracking objects by pairing each object with one mark, and used the leftover-stone method to identify a boat that had not returned. They first mixed up spacing with quantity, but later corrected this by making pairs and noticing that no bindi or bangle was left over. At home, try pairing everyday objects one-to-one, such as spoons and plates, and ask what it means if one is left over.
